chapter: Growing up with jazz in Belfast
title: Where the Belfast band played, and Belfast's approach to jazz
summary: Belfast's small wartime jazz scene, the polite society band, its members, and the dance jobs it played.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Then, and then mostly instead of playing like the clubs in London and some of the other towns in England, they would just spot around like, you know, like spotting around here, huh?

Yes, they'd play anywhere. Uh-huh. They had one regular weekly job on a Saturday night at the, uh, the, I forget the name of the damn school they played at. They played in the gymnasium. Um, the Royal Academy, Belfast Royal Academy, BRA, one of the biggest schools over there.

Uh, every Saturday, but they play anywhere. They've, they've been playing at the boat club. Uh, it's very different to some of the boat clubs I've played in over here. It's, it's not a big bar, you know, more like across, you know, kind of thing. Yeah. All the mill girls go over there. Belfast is an industrial town. Uh-huh. Oh, it's very different in Belfast, if you're interested. I mean, Belfast is kind of a backwater, but it's very different. The approach to jazz over there always seemed to me, this is before I left, it might have changed, but it always seemed to be, uh, much more like here in that they were anxious to satisfy the dancers, the people who paid their few shillings to get in at all costs, rather than having this big pretentious, uh, we're going to revive the original New Orleans jazz at all costs, even though nobody can, uh, put their finger on what the original New Orleans jazz is. I mean, London, of course in London you've got anything to satisfy all tastes, I suppose. Yeah. And I went to London, in my last year of high school, I went to London, I heard Ken Collier's band in 1949, the Crane River Jazz Band. Of course he, Ken Collier's got kind of a name, he came over here and all.
